question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 0 \\ -2 & -1 & 1 \\ 7 & -5 & -4\end{aligned}],\,J=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}1 & a & ∗ \\ 1 & b & ∗ \\ 1 & c & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices above. Given that $A=PJ{P}^{-1}$ is a Jordan canonical decomposition of $A,$ find the value of $a-b.$
question.worked_solution:
Since the Jordan matrix $J$ has a single $3\times 3$ Jordan block corresponding to $\lambda =-2,$ the columns of $P$ form the following chain: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3}\overset{A+2I\,}{\to }{v}_{2}\overset{A+2I\,}{\to }{v}_{1}\overset{A+2I\,}{\to }0\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain that 

- the first column of $P$ corresponds to the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ of the eigenvalue $\lambda =-2,$

- the second column of $P$ corresponds to the vector ${v}_{2}$ such that $(A+2I){v}_{2}={v}_{1}.$

Now, computing $A+2I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A+2I & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 0 \\ -2 & -1 & 1 \\ 7 & -5 & -4\end{aligned}]+2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 1 \\ 7 & -5 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the matrix equation $(A+2I){v}_{2}={v}_{1}$ is equivalent to the system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 7 & -5 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-7){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we have ${x}_{2}={x}_{3}-3.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}-({x}_{3}-3)=1\,⟹\,{x}_{1}={x}_{3}-2.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{3}-2 \\ {x}_{3}-3 \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{3}=0,$ we get  

$$
{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a-b=-2-(-3)=1.$
